chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In the case of an ox that was stubborn (difficult to slaughter), a group of men rushed it with their swords, and they slaughtered it. They went to Ali (peace be upon him) and he said:
This is a valid slaughter, a proper one, and its meat is permissible.
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of an ox considered halal if it is slaughtered by rushing it with swords because it was stubborn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the slaughter of a stubborn ox by a group using swords, emphasizing that the collective action suffices for validity even if the precise ritual formula is not individually recited. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'dhakāh' (slaughter) being determined by the act of cutting the throat vessels rather than strict adherence to a single slaughterer, ensuring the meat remains halal for consumption.
